meta.title: Synthetic wheat lines show heritable changes in root architecture under mild drought
affiliations: 1Department of Plant Sciences, Example University, Exampletown, EX1 2AB, UK. 2Institute of Soil Ecology, Example Institute, Sample City, EX3 4CD, UK.

abstractHtml: Root system architecture determines water capture in dry soils. We grew 240 recombinant inbred lines under two watering regimes and measured rooting depth, lateral root density and xylem vessel diameter. Lines carrying the RtA1 allele showed a 19% increase in deep-root fraction under mild drought, and this difference persisted across two seasons. Transcript profiling of root tips identified a small module of 34 genes whose expression tracked the deep-root phenotype.

blocks.html: Wheat yields under rain-fed conditions depend strongly on how quickly roots reach subsoil water. Breeding for deep roots has been attempted for decades with mixed success1, in part because root traits are difficult to phenotype at scale2. Recent work suggests that relatively few loci control the partitioning of root mass with depth3, 4.

Here we combine a field trial, a controlled-environment experiment and transcript profiling to ask whether a single allele at the RtA1 locus is sufficient to shift root mass downward without a yield penalty.

Across both watering regimes, rooting depth at anthesis ranged from 41 to 96 cm (Fig. 1a). The distribution was bimodal in the drought treatment and unimodal in the well-watered treatment (Fig. 1b). Lines grouped by RtA1 genotype differed in the deep-root fraction (Fig. 2).

Transcript profiling of the top 2 cm of root identified 34 genes differentially expressed between
        genotype classes, of which 21 were also differentially expressed in the second season
        (Supplementary Table 3).

Our results are consistent with a model in which the RtA1 allele alters the timing of lateral root initiation rather than the total number of lateral roots5. The absence of a yield penalty in the drought treatment is encouraging, although the trial covered only two seasons.

Several caveats apply. Phenotyping was destructive, so we could not follow individual roots over
        time. The transcript module is correlative, and the causal variant remains to be identified.

Seeds were sown in October 2024 and 2025 in a randomised block design with four replicates. Plots
        received either ambient rainfall or a rain-out shelter from stem elongation onward.

Roots were sampled with a 6 cm diameter auger to 100 cm depth in 10 cm increments, washed over a
        2 mm sieve and scanned at 600 dpi.
